You are a financial-analysis assistant operating in a tool-enabled environment.  Read the background below, then use any combination of the available tools whenever they help you ground your reasoning in structured data.  When you have enough information, return only the final answer as a number (no explanations).

BACKGROUND (scenario – narrative excerpts only, no tables)
----------------------------------------------------------------
2009 levels, we returned a portion of these assets to active service.  At the end of 2010 we continued to maintain in storage approximately 17 % of our multiple-purpose locomotives and 14 % of our freight-car inventory, reflecting our ability to effectively leverage our assets as volumes return to our network.

Fuel prices generally increased throughout 2010 as the economy improved.  Our average diesel fuel price per gallon increased nearly 20 % from January to December of 2010, driven by higher crude-oil barrel prices and conversion spreads.  Compared to 2009, our diesel fuel price per gallon consumed increased 31 %, driving operating expenses up by $566 million (excluding any impact from year-over-year volume increases).  To partially offset the effect of higher fuel prices, we reduced our consumption rate by 3 % during the year, saving approximately 27 million gallons of fuel.  The use of newer, more fuel-efficient locomotives; increased use of distributed locomotive power; fuel-conservation programs; and efficient network operations and asset utilization all contributed to this improvement.

Cash generated by operating activities (adjusted for the reclassification of our receivables-securitization facility) totaled $4.5 billion, yielding record free cash flow of $1.4 billion in 2010.  Free cash flow is defined as cash provided by operating activities (adjusted for the reclassification of our receivables-securitization facility), less cash used in investing activities and dividends paid.  We believe free cash flow is important in evaluating our financial performance and measures our ability to generate cash without additional external financings.  Free cash flow should be considered in addition to, rather than as a substitute for, cash provided by operating activities.

We will continue using a multi-faceted approach to safety, utilizing technology, risk assessment, quality control, and training, and engaging our employees.  Reducing grade-crossing incidents is a critical aspect of our safety programs, and we will continue our efforts to maintain and close crossings; install video cameras on locomotives; and educate the public and law-enforcement agencies about crossing safety.
----------------------------------------------------------------

• list_companies() → List[str]
    Return all company names in the structured finance database.

• list_statement_types(company_name: str, year: int) → List[str]
    For the specified company and year, list available statement types (e.g. "cashflow").

• list_items_in_statement(company_name: str, year: int, statement_type: str) → List[str]
    List every item name stored in that statement.

• fetch_item_amount(company_name: str, year: int, statement_type: str, item_name: str, as_unit: str = "raw"|"million"|"billion") → float
    Retrieve the numeric amount for an item, optionally converting units.

• compute_ratio(numerator: float, denominator: float, precision: int = 2) → float
    Convenience helper that divides two numbers and rounds the result.

• get_average_item_across_years(company_name: str, item_name: str, as_unit: str = "billion") → float
    Returns the average value of an item across all years for the company (may not be relevant to every task).

Use these tools as needed; you can chain them together in multiple steps.

TASK (question to answer)
----------------------------------------------------------------
In 2010, what was the ratio of the cash generated by operating activities to the free cash flow of $1.4 billion?
----------------------------------------------------------------
Remember: return only the final numeric ratio (e.g., 3.21).

We believe free cash flow is important in evaluating our financial performance and measures our ability to generate cash without additional external financings.  Free cash flow should be considered in addition to, rather than as a substitute for, cash provided by operating activities.

We will continue using a multi-faceted approach to safety, utilizing technology, risk assessment, quality control, and training, and engaging our employees.
